fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Circular Driveway; Landscaped Area; Open Terrain
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Open Terrain
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions of the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to help responders locate the turn-in at night or in reduced visibility.
• Keep the full width of the driveway clear of overhanging branches to allow passage of fire apparatus and ambulances.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the driveway to maintain a clear line of sight from the road to the residence.
• Keep the circular driveway fully passable and free of parked vehicles so arriving apparatus can pull through without reversing.
• Designate a staging area on the circular driveway where a second arriving unit can position without blocking the primary access route.
• Thin dense vegetation bordering the driveway to reduce conditions that could slow or stop responder access if fire moves onto the property.
• Keep the circular driveway surface in a condition that supports the weight of heavy emergency vehicles year-round.
• Post a clearly visible address sign at the residence itself so responders arriving on scene can confirm they have reached the correct structure.
• Identify and mark any secondary path across open terrain that could serve as an alternate way out if the main driveway becomes blocked.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Shrubs; Open Green Space; Long Driveway; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Trees; Open Terrain; Scattered Shrubs; Limited Turnaround Area; Single Access Route
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the house on all sides.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure to open up space between tree canopies and the roofline.
• Remove shrubs growing beneath tree canopies close to the house so fire cannot climb from ground level into the trees.
• Clear a wider gap between the nearest shrub clusters and the walls of the structure.
• Cut back any shrubs or low branches that overhang or lean toward the house.
• Keep the full length of the driveway clear of overhanging branches so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Widen any narrow sections of the driveway where vegetation has grown inward from the sides.
• Clear a turnaround area at or near the end of the driveway large enough for a fire truck to reverse direction.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible to emergency responders approaching from the road.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from shrubs growing near the structure.
• Maintain the open green space near the house by keeping grass cut short and removing any dead growth.
• Thin shrub clusters on the uphill or windward sides of the house before addressing lower-priority sides.
• Keep a clear, unobstructed path around all sides of the structure for firefighter movement.
